security_privacy_cost_impact: The first third-party code in the repository: 178 lockfile packages, installed with --ignore-scripts from the npm registry with sha512 integrity, under licences §3.4/2 accepts or Amendment 2026-10-12 names. No provider SDK, no credential, no customer data, no provider call. Next.js telemetry is off in CI and in the config. One entry (fsevents, macOS-only, optional) carries the registry's hasInstallScript flag and runs nothing; it goes to A1 under §8/8.
compatibility_impact: No contract changes. The tooling tier is unchanged and npm run check stays dependency-free; the application checks run in their own CI job.
known_limitations: RFC-2026-029 §8/4 asks for lint errors; with ESLint deferred by the Owner the boundaries and §2.1/3 are held by scripts/verify-app-boundaries.mjs, which in CI (--require-parser) reads every file through TypeScript's parser (the Owner allowed that import, 2026-10-12T07:24:27Z); without node_modules (npm run check) a dependency-free text reader runs, and the `any` rule is held only by the parsed run. Build configuration is admitted only in the shapes scripts/app-dependency-allowlist.json's $comment lists (next.config, vitest.config, postcss.config as literal data with allowlisted keys; Babel and vite configs, every PostCSS search name but postcss.config.*, anything under a .config/ directory and any tracked .env* but .env.example refused, names matched in any letter case; every workspace's scripts pinned to the allowlist (apps/web: build = next build); NODE_OPTIONS is empty in the application job). After next build, scripts/verify-app-build-graph.mjs fails on any file the build output names from outside apps/web/** and src/modules/** or any package not reachable from the allowlist; the shapes, refusals, pinned workspace scripts and empty NODE_OPTIONS hold what configuration can make a build tool load; code the repository itself runs in CI after the guard (a test, a page at prerender, build-time code) could still write files or change the output, and that residual is held by review of every pull request, not by a check (A1-257-10). CI runs the guard again immediately before the build.

The build-graph check reads server traces, source maps and server/build module ids; it does not see code that runs during the build, and client-only code (a browser condition, possibly next/dynamic with ssr: false, not measured) is not traced, and browser source maps are not enabled because they would publish the source. Its reachable-package set includes the dev tooling's dependency tree. It is measured on macOS; CI on Linux is its first run there and fails closed if paths are written differently.
The release-age and audit steps read the registry at CI time; a registry outage fails them.

Locally, npm run check fails after a next build because the secret scanner walks apps/web/.next/; delete it first. CI is not affected (the build runs in the application job). The scanner's owner, WP-0A-A0-003, owes a decision (R0-257-3).

Until the application job is a required status check of main, a red application job does not block a merge in GitHub; the Owner directed A0 to add it through gh api after this PR merges, changing nothing else. A0 presses only on all jobs green.
